approachQuestion.prompt:
Maintenance dates in a range

An event occurs on every integer date divisible by positive k. Given an inclusive integer date range [L,R], return the number of event dates in it. Date zero is divisible by every positive k and must be counted when present.

Example 1: L=-5,R=-1,k=3 -> 1, for date -3.
Example 2: L=-3,R=3,k=3 -> 3, for -3,0,3.
Example 3: L=1,R=2,k=5 -> 0.

Constraints and assumptions: -10^18 <= L <= R <= 10^18; 1 <= k <= 10^9. Signed integer division in the language truncates toward zero. Return one exact signed 64-bit count. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Implement mathematical floor division by correcting negative nonzero remainders after truncated division. Return floorDiv(R,k)-floorDiv(L-1,k).
options.feedback: The difference counts the integer multiples with quotient between the two boundaries, including zero. Correcting truncation is essential when boundaries are negative.

options.text: Use exact mathematical ceil(L/k) to find first=k*ceil(L/k). Return 0 if first>R, otherwise floor((R-first)/k)+1. Implement ceil by incrementing truncated division when its remainder is positive.
options.feedback: This finds the first legal event even for negative L. Subsequent events are spaced by k; R-first is nonnegative, so the remaining division is unambiguous.

options.text: Return truncated(R/k)-truncated((L-1)/k), without correcting negative values.
options.feedback: For L=-5,R=-1,k=3 this returns 0-(-2)=2 rather than 1; truncation is not floor for -1/3.
For L=0,R=0,k=3 this returns 0 although date 0 is an event; alignment with multiples matters.

feedback.reason: Count multiples across signed interval boundaries with mathematical floor division.
details: Implement floorDiv(x,k) by truncated q=x/k, decrementing q once if x<0 and x rem k is nonzero. Return floorDiv(R,k)-floorDiv(L-1,k).

Count multiples through R minus multiples before L using mathematical floor division. Truncation toward zero is wrong for negative dates with a nonzero remainder. Include L via L-1 in the lower boundary.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (floor-difference). Let S=R-L+1 be the range length; division is a unit-cost word operation. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

feedback.reason: Two corrected floor divisions count dates without visiting individual dates.
details: The analyzed method performs two fixed-size floor-division corrections and a subtraction. It never visits individual dates. L-1 is at least -10^18-1, and the count is at most 2*10^18+1, safely within signed 64-bit range.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.

“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct: two boundary quotients and a fixed correction.
“O(S) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes scanning dates, which the method avoids.
“O(log(S + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The method performs no search or repeated reduction.
“O(1) time, O(S) auxiliary space”: No event-date list or bitmap is allocated.
